source_text: Secundum autem librum expositione Apostoli argumentis Augustini ex adverso positis pro ea, quam suppeditavit veritas, facultate complevi; atque ideo nunc ad libri eius ordinem revertamur.
pass_a_gloss: But the second book I have filled with the exposition of the Apostle, with Augustine's arguments placed from the opposite, by the faculty which truth supplied; and therefore now let us return to the order of his book.

lemmas.lexica: LS facultas; Blaise ability to choose

pass_b_english: I filled the second book with an exposition of the apostle, setting Augustine’s arguments against it, to the extent truth supplied me the ability. So now let us return to the sequence of his book.

choices.why: Paul in Julian's citations; keep Apostle not 'Paul' unless Paulus is written.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
